To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) fully human monoclonal antibodies against vaccinia virus (VACV) and rabbitpox virus (RPXV) can prevent or treat lethal poxviral infections in rabbits and severe combined immunodeficient (SCID) mice; 2) fully human monoclaonal antibodies against vaccinia H5L and B5R can prevent or treat smallpox in SCID mice and rabbitpox in rabbits.

fully human monoclonal antibodies against vaccinia H5 and B5, targeting both the mature and extracellular envelop forms of the virus, provide significant protection against lethal poxviral infections in mice and rabbits.
(1) combination hmAb therapy provides significant protection against VACV infection and disease in SCID mice and (2) hmAb therapy provides 100% protection against RPXV disease in rabbits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel therapeutic approach for the treatment of poxvirus disease in both animals and humans.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for use in the prevention and/or treatment of smallpox and other poxvirus diseases.
the development and evaluation of fully human mAbs as potential therapeutics to treat and protect humans against lethal smallpox infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of two fully human monoclonal antibodies against vaccinia virus (VACV), H3 and B5, provides significant therapeutic efficacy in severe combined immunodeficient (SCID) mice and rabbitpox (rabbit poxvirus) infected rabbits, and is an excellent candidate for use as an anti-poxvirus bioweapon countermeasure.
the hmAbs are effective in the treatment of smallpox in both rabbits and mice.
the hmAbs are effective at preventing and treating lethal poxviral infections in rabbits and immunodeficient mice, and are therefore potential therapeutics for humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of combination hmAb prophylactic therapy may be a viable option for preventing or treating poxvirus diseases.
the use of human monoclonal antibodies (hmAbs) for smallpox and monkeypox prophylaxis and treatment has been demonstrated to be effective in animal models.
we developed a novel approach to the treatment of smallpox and related poxvirus disease in humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
combination mAb therapy is effective at preventing or treating lethal poxviral infections in rabbits.
combination hmAb therapy may be an important tool in controlling a smallpox outbreak.
combination hmAb prophylactic and therapeutic treatment of smallpox disease is feasible and effective.
